Add an Exit Game option that frees the seat and returns to the lobby

New "leave" WebSocket message, handled in consumers.py: if a hand is
live and the leaving seat hasn't folded/busted/never been dealt in,
it's folded out first -- through the real apply_action_and_advance()
path if it's actually their turn (so the turn properly advances and
any resulting showdown gets persisted same as a normal fold), or just
flagged folded in place otherwise. The seat is then cleared (player,
cards) and immediately re-seated with a bot via seat_bot_if_needed(),
the same mechanism a table's empty seats always go through -- so no
seat is ever left "owned by nobody" for advance_turn() or blind
posting to stall on, and the vacated spot becomes eligible again for
the next real player to join (same eviction rule as any other bot
seat: before the next deal, not mid-hand).

The server acks with {"type": "left"} sent directly to the leaving
connection; play.html's new Exit button sends "leave" and waits for
that ack before redirecting to "/", rather than racing the message
against the page navigating away.

Caught and fixed one real bug while verifying live: the leave handler
was unconditionally re-dispatching a bot task for whatever seat
currently held the turn, even when leaving didn't change whose turn
it was -- duplicating the dispatch already scheduled from whenever
that turn actually started, which crashed the second one once the
first had already acted. Now only dispatches when leaving is what
actually advanced the turn.

Verified live: left while NOT on turn (seat folded in place, bot-filled,
no duplicate dispatch, confirmed clean through the next two real bot
actions) and left WHILE on turn (folded via the real path, turn
correctly advanced). Full suite 64/64, JS syntax and Django checks
clean.

commit.message:
feat: carry Discord voice UDP through the proxy with a scoped TUN

Voice never went through the proxy: HTTP/SOCKS-TCP cannot carry UDP,
Chromium ignores --proxy-server for it, and Discord has no TURN fallback,
so every call left direct and came back throttled - the 5000<->100ms cycle.

A vendored sing-box (v1.12.25) now owns a local TUN that receives only
/32 host routes for Discord voice-server IPs, learned from the relay's
own CONNECT lines and screened against Cloudflare/private ranges - never
a default route, so game ping never touches it - and forwards them over
SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE. The elevated half is this exe re-launched with
--voice-pipe=<nonce>, talking to the app over a named pipe; the proxy is
probed for UDP support before any UAC prompt appears.

Add request modes (Chat/Manage/Analyst/Simulator) and wire the race simulator

Lily answered from the game docs by default because every tool and every
matching doc was in play on every turn. A mode now narrows one turn:

- Chat (default): web + everyday tools, no game docs

- Analyst: game docs, table/affinity calculators, collection
- Simulator: veterans and the race simulator

Typing "mode" shows four buttons; "simulator mode" etc. switch. Both are
handled in the router, never by the model. The mode lives in the session.
Tools are filtered by ToolSpec.category, a tool from another mode is refused
if the model asks for it, and Chat offers Analyst once when a message names a
game doc.

Simulator Mode:
- sim_service.py is the single door into the Simulation folder (sys.path set
  once, capped runs, worker thread, compact summary that keeps the model-limits
  caveat ahead of the output cap)
- tools: sim_list_veterans, sim_find_skill, sim_list_courses, sim_run
- veterans and results are stored per user in the database (LilyAiMemory/Veteran),
  not in the global Veteran/ folder, so users are isolated and a Render deploy
  no longer wipes them
- screenshots in Simulator Mode go through VeteranIntake; elsewhere they still
  go to the career review

Also fixes VeteranStore failing at import: the method named `list` shadowed the
builtin inside the class body, breaking the `list[...]` annotation on `find`.

Fix the Flatpak rollback watchdog missing a crash in Game Mode

Found testing on a real Steam Deck. The watchdog was launched through a
flatpak-spawn client that stays alive inside the old sandbox for as long
as the watchdog runs, so the old instance stayed listed in flatpak ps and
a crash of the new version was never seen. The same lingering instance
could also read as the new version stopping, rolling back a good update.

observe mode now remembers which instances existed before and judges only
the one its own launch creates, and the watchdog is started through a
throwaway host shell under setsid so the old sandbox can exit.
